title: Warehouse source resources must yield bounded pages, never one whole-report list
answers: Bing Ads sync OOM kills the data warehouse worker pod
Why does a large source sync exhaust memory even though the batcher caps batch size?
How should a warehouse source yield large reports or tables?
body:
Each item a source yields is materialized whole; the batcher only caps what it accumulates BETWEEN items, so one oversized item sets the activity's peak memory by itself.
- Sources must yield bounded pages (list of rows), not one list of every row. Bing Ads: `REPORT_PAGE_ROWS = 50_000` in `products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/sources/bing_ads/utils.py`, used by `iter_csv_row_pages`.
- Paging keeps batch and file sizes unchanged; the batcher still regroups pages.
- Each layer must stay streaming: `BingAdsClient.get_performance_report` and `get_data_by_resource` in `bing_ads/client.py` use `yield from`. Collecting pages back into a list (or yielding the generator itself) re-materializes the report.
- The OOM kills the pod, taking co-tenant team syncs down, and the schema retries and repeats it.
- No generic guard exists yet against a source yielding one oversized item.
applies: Any warehouse_sources source that yields large API/report results (temporal/data_imports/sources/*).
